To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

conversion of ISW into densified RDF (dRDF), along with compost production, can be a feasible alternative for waste management in PIAT UGM, provided that no restriction to the processed waste and steady flow of d RDF product to end users.
the conversion of combustible and organic waste from ISW into d R DF and compost is a feasible alternative to manage the waste.
the production of dRDF and the sale of compost can be a good alternative for waste management in the PIAT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
ISW management, which is an urgent issue for UGM.
the feasibility of dRDF and its potential to be used as an alternative fuel in PIAT, UGM.
the environmental and economic feasibility of ISW conversion into dRDF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conversion of ISW into d-RDF and compost would be a feasible option to reduce the ISW volume, to reduce environmental impacts of ISW disposal, and to generate economic benefits.
the production of dRDF and organic compost from UGM ISW is an effective alternative for waste management and a potential source for renewable energy.
dRDF and its compost are environmentally and economically feasible as a waste management alternative for UGM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conversion of combustible waste into dRDF is an environmentally friendly option for waste treatment and energy generation, provided that the waste is separated properly, and the dRDF is used for electricity generation with emission control.
the conversion of ISW into d-RDF and compost would not only reduce environmental impacts, but would also be profitable.
the conversion of waste into dRDF with compost production is a promising alternative to the current practice of waste management in PIAT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conversion of ISW to dRDF combined composting could be a viable option for waste management in PIAT UGM, as well as in other institutions.
the conversion of combustible waste into RDF and compost could be an option to reduce environmental impacts and improve economic value of waste management.
dRDF and organic waste compost can be used to substitute coal and fertilizer in Indonesia.
